title: Probe diary & tally sheet — Mira
summary: Lightweight personal tracker for short-run inference probes. Captures quick tallies (latency/cost/cache) and my incremental notes so I can revisit without hunting through Slack/PRs.
how_to_use: 1) Append a new row every time you run a short probe (<= 5m). 2) Keep 'session_id' stable across retries. 3) Use the quick notes field for immediate hypotheses + action items. 4) I keep this in users/ because it's messy and transient.

notes_freeform:
Quick notes (unpolished):
- Observed that cache hit rate correlates non-linearly with p95; below ~60% p95 balloons. Hypothesis: background eviction pattern causes cache churn.
- When testing batching=8 (S20260120-D) throughput jumped ~4x but 99th percentile latency went through the roof. For user-facing RPCs, cap batch size at 2 or route to dedicated pool.
- Cost calc I use: cost_per_1k = (raw infra cost estimate per inference * tokens) normalized; very rough, need proper multiply by token count.
- Quick commands: 
  > ./tools/collect-latency.sh --session S20260228-H --out /tmp/S20260228-H.json
  > jq '.p95, .avg' /tmp/S20260228-H.json
- Observability hooks: tie session_id to trace id in telemetry (ticket: LINEAR-456) so I can jump from this sheet to flamegraphs.
- Unresolved: why S20260202-E had surprisingly high quality for one prompt family. Might be sampling/higher temp by accident. Re-run with deterministic seeds.
decisions_and_actions:

- Keep rw-7b-int8 as primary cheap baseline for feature experiments (low cost, acceptable quality).
- Use rw-14b-pt for long-context tests and rollout guardrails.
